wa_golden_age.notes: The prominent left-facing, left-arching corner. Delicate thin corner climbing leads to a burly 4–5 in layback; at the wedged chockstones move left to rest, then power through a short physical roof. The only pitch that needs the #5 cam; it can be left at the anchor and collected on the way down.

Easy climbing leads to a physical crux over another small roof. Face climbing then gains a shallow left-leaning crack that fades out, ending in a hard lunge to a ledge; easy climbing up a left-facing corner finishes on Smoke Break Ledge.
Climb a ramp and across a golden panel; a technical, reachy crux passes flakes and leads to a steep ramp and the belay. The stone on this pitch is some of the cleanest on the route.
The crux pitch. Pumpy laybacking reaches a rest, then launch right through an overlap into a powerful traverse, follow a bathtub-shaped rail, and a second crimpy crux guards the belay.
A tricky mantle off the belay leads to an exposed hand-traverse crack, then an awkward mantle onto the belay stance.

A pleasant flake leads to a thin bolted crux, then steep jugs go out to the apex of the overhangs and a burly hand-crack roof. Continue straight up until a hand traverse right reaches the belay. A little loose in places, but the belay and the rope run out of the line of fire.

Climb toward the arete on crisp crimps on solid golden rock, then move left to a final cruxy mantle. From the top, rappel the route with one 70 m rope; the second rappel anchor from the top is off to the left of the line.

wa_marvin_s_ear.notes: Scramble up to a high first bolt with fun stemming on mostly good rock higher up.
Edges and slab moves more or less straight up from the belay.
Walk/scramble along ledges, clipping one bolt on the way to the anchor.
A sustained line of 9 bolts up the broad, golden-granite ridge crest, with pumpy dihedral moves easing off just before the two-bolt anchor.
Bolts trend left toward the end of the pitch to reach the next belay.
The technical crux: a cruxy move over a bulge into another sustained, cruxy section; extend a few draws to manage rope drag.
A cool traverse left, then up through a fun corner to the anchor just below the summit.

wa_mojo_rising.notes: Starts on the obvious bolt line about 20 ft downhill from the chockstone feature, left of the first pitch of the Northwest Face. Runout 5.6 leads to the first bolt, then a bolted face. The first ascent used aid (A0) here; the bolts are spaced too far apart to aid or French-free easily.
Aid up a thin, very flared seam past one bolt, then one last 5.6 move to the anchor. The placements are fiddly: small cams, offsets and brass nuts are the useful pieces. Not yet reported free.

From the right side of the ledge, climb a short wide crack (5.10a), then cut back left into an alcove with a steep corner crack above a sloping ledge. Aid the seam, where a blown piece could deck you on the ledge. Free climb the crack to a foot rail and make a hard traverse left to the belay. Could go free as a stemming problem.
The Skywalker Traverse. The first ascent tension-traversed and lowered out onto Skywalker ledge (5.8 A0). Plan how you will protect the follower on the sideways moves.

An awkward 10a seam leads right off the belay into a corner. Climb carefully up and around a huge block that is completely detached, keeping the rope and the follower out of its fall line. Then good 5.9 finger crack climbing leads to a belay on hand and finger pieces.
Climb blocky terrain and pass through some trees to reach the crest of the Southwest Rib.

Finish up the well-traveled Southwest Rib to the summit, easy ground that parties either simul-climb or pitch out. To bail instead, rappel the first three pitches with a single 60 m rope from the bolted anchors.
